before: Your little one has their own version of that last question: "Big fuckity whoopty doo. What are you gonna do for me?" They actually want to know, though I think the first answer may be that you keep loving them, even while they don't believe you. Then their trust can grow from the stuff back in "Not Every Hero Wears A Cape," like hearing out the sarcasm, or finally opening that envelope.

brief:

The article already has relaxing in it: slower exhales and a little self-massage when your solar plexus is tight, "take a breath or three", and "Take that breather you earned". Point back in a few words if it helps; don't teach it again.
- the guide: "It cannot decide whether the complaint is true, assign guilt, or create trust by itself." Keep all three, and keep "by itself": relaxing can't tell you whether their complaint is true, can't say who's guilty, and can't make trust happen on its own.
